evidence: Conditional vacuum scalings and continued-operation cost allowances. Ambient pressure does not select a plant shutdown date. No retrofit quotation or retained-market forecast.

vacuum.leak_rule: Illustrative controlled equal-temperature molecular conductance: Q_leak=C*(P_ambient-P_target). Constant C is not extrapolated to real openings across flow regimes. Internal gas release remains fixed.

continuation.output_rule: Continuation years51–100 each assume the reference 63.7Mt/year output at unchanged prices, quality and orders. No demand loss or product-mix optimization is solved.
continuation.cost_rule: Up-front retrofit is paid at the end ofyear50. Extra annual costs are paid at year ends51–100 and include all extra pumping, enclosure upkeep/replacement, downtime losses and delivery burdens within the allowance. No added salvage credit. Costs are assumed, not inferred from pressure.

boundaries: The original50-year liquidation case remains a stress test, not a pressure-predicted closure.100-year continuation is a conditional alternative, not a selected commissioning schedule.

The incremental decision compares continuing an existing plant against liquidating it; original investment NPV also includes the initial capital. Debt/refinancing and mandatory equity payouts require separate cash funding.

Price, order and freight retention must be tested against competitors. A positive incremental NPV does not by itself establish liquidity, market access, safe enclosure design or a whole-project atmospheric-delay benefit.

The constant-effective-speed pump model is an ideal transient diagnostic. Real pumping speed, ultimate pressure, gas species, conductance, desorption, heating and process vapours affect performance. Pressure loads do not translate proportionally into complete chamber cost.
Gradual atmospheric loading affects launch and production separately. A loss of ambient process vacuum is neither a ban on pumped processing nor an automatic full-atmosphere freight tariff.
